newsitem.title: USA: Royal Oak will defend against injunction.
newsitem.headline: Royal Oak will defend against injunction.

text.p: Royal Oak Mines Inc said on Thursday it would vigorously defend against an injunction sought today by lawyers for the Tsay Keh Dene native group, to stop Royal Oak from proceeding with construction of the Kemess South mine site in British Columbia.

Royal Oak said it had fully complied with and relied upon the regulatory requirements for project approval from the provincial and federal governments and it was proceeding with construction of the project and clearing of the power line corridor in reliance on those approvals.

"After a lengthy permitting process, the Kemess project and related power line were issued Project Approval Certificates to proceed, as well as valid licences of occupation and approval to cut the power line corridor," Royal Oak said in a statement.

It added: "In regard to the various First Nations Bands in and around the project area, the company has been engaged in consultation with the bands for several years and has made every effort to make contracts and employment opportunities related to the project available to the bands."
